title: Cargo Complaint Help Desk
text: AAI has introduced a Help Desk at the Cargo Complex to help users resolve day-to-day problems, complaints, and grievances quickly at airports. Grievances can be submitted in writing to the In-charge at the Air Cargo Complex or the Airport Director for prompt action and appropriate response.

title: Complaint Response Timeline
text: If a customer experiences undue delay, they may contact the concerned duty officer, who is available round-the-clock, for grievance redressal. AAI acknowledges written complaints within 2 working days and responds to such communications within 15 working days of receipt. Complaint registers are maintained with Duty Officers and suggestion boxes are placed at conspicuous locations at all Cargo Terminals.

title: Escalation for Non-Redressal of Cargo Complaints
text: If a grievance or complaint is not redressed satisfactorily, the office of the Executive Director (Cargo) or General Manager (Cargo) at AAI Headquarters, Delhi, can be contacted. Contact details: Tel. No. 011-24657930 / 24657919, FAX No. 24657929.

title: Electronic Transaction Registration
text: Any exporter, importer, Customs House Agent, or airline wishing to transact electronically with AAI must register with AAI. Registration requires filling a physical registration form with relevant documents and submitting it to AAI. Users must provide a valid email address and phone number so AAI can communicate User ID and password allocation, and are advised to change the assigned password immediately after receipt.

title: Free Period for Cargo Clearance
text: Exporters are allowed a 12-hour free period to process and hand over customs-cleared export cargo to the custodian at the cargo terminal. Imported goods can be cleared within 48 hours from the time of arrival without payment of any demurrage charges.

title: Demurrage Charge Waiver Process
text: Applications for waiver of demurrage charges must be submitted within 15 calendar days from the date the customs 'Passed out of Charge' order is issued. Delays beyond 15 days but within 30 days may be considered by the Airport Director/GM(Cargo) with reasons for condonation of delay and local finance concurrence. AAI acknowledges waiver requests submitted by hand on the spot, and processes applications within 15 days if handled locally, or 30 days if referred to AAI Headquarters, provided all relevant documents are furnished.

title: Documents Required for Demurrage Waiver
text: A waiver application should be made by the consignee/shipper within 15 days of the consignment being passed 'Out of Charge' or given a 'Let Export Order' by Customs, addressed to the Airport Director/GM(Cargo)/Deputy GM(Cargo) at the respective airport. It must include legible photocopies of the Air Waybill (AWB), Bill of Entry with Customs Examination Report, Shipping Bill, and Detention Certificate from a statutory authority if applicable. The consignee/shipper can also appeal to the AAI Appellate Authority for reconsideration.

title: Cargo Damage/Loss Claim Process
text: Claim cases for damage, pilferage, or theft received from consignees/consignors are registered in the claim register at the Cargo Administration Section. Required documents include a copy of the AWB/HAWB, invoice, packing list, segregation report (if applicable), Bill of Entry, Joint Survey Report, claim bill, weight/loss documentation, and an FIR application.

title: Cargo Claim Settlement Process
text: If cargo is received in good condition but damaged while in AAI custody, a claim is lodged with AAI's underwriters, with facilitation for survey at AAI premises. Once documents are furnished, a formal claim is lodged with the underwriter. If settled, the claimant must provide a letter of subrogation confirming no other claim was made, after which the settlement amount is sent to the Accounts Department for release to the claimant.

title: Cargo Terminal Penalty Provisions
text: Any offence or violation by users of the cargo terminal not otherwise specified attracts a maximum penal action of Rs. 500, subject to a minimum of Rs. 100 per instance, with approval of the Head/In-charge of the Cargo Department.

title: Baggage Vigilance During Security Screening
text: Passengers are advised to keep strict vigil on their baggage while it is placed on the X-ray baggage inspection system, and to immediately check their items at the time of retrieval. Any loss detected must be reported immediately to the security in-charge of the security hold area, along with representatives of the airline and airport operator.

title: Baggage Retrieval Precaution
text: When retrieving registered baggage from the conveyor belt or arrival hall, passengers must verify their own baggage by tallying the serial number on the coupon given at check-in against the tag number on the baggage.

title: Responsibility for Lodging FIR on Loss
text: It is the responsibility of the passenger or visitor to lodge an FIR with the concerned state police for any loss, since it is a law and order matter.

title: CCTV Footage Retention for Loss Reports
text: CCTV camera recordings are retained for only thirty days, so any report of loss must be made immediately to the concerned airport's Airport Director.

title: Scope of AAI Responsibility for Baggage Loss
text: AAI only investigates losses that occur within the airport building or security hold area. For any loss occurring in a passenger's registered (checked-in) baggage, the concerned airline must be approached instead of AAI.

title: Where to Report a Loss or Security Issue at the Airport
text: A passenger or visitor who notices the loss of any item should report the matter to the Airport Director, Airport Terminal Manager, Chief Airport Security Officer, or the Shift In-charge of CISF/Police.

title: General Security Precautions for Travelers
text: Travelers should report suspicious persons to the security agency or terminal manager, remain vigilant so no unauthorized person can tamper with their baggage, and never accept items to carry onboard from unknown persons, as these could be prohibited items or explosives, potentially leading to action against the passenger.

title: CISF Deployment at Airports
text: AAI has deployed CISF (Central Industrial Security Force) to carry out airport security functions at 52 AAI airports and civil enclaves. At the remaining operational airports and civil enclaves, State Police carries out these functions.

title: Directorate of Security Contact Details
text: The Directorate of Security is located at 'C' Wing, 2nd Floor, R.G. Bhawan, Safdarjung Airport, New Delhi. Contact details for the Director (Security): Telephone (Office) 011-24616203, Fax 011-24690324.

title: Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS)
text: The Bureau of Civil Aviation Security (BCAS) is the designated agency of the Government of India under the Ministry of Civil Aviation responsible for regulations, procedures, and directions covering security aspects of aircraft operations and airports in India. Their instructions must be complied with by both airlines and airports.

title: User Development Fee (UDF) and Development Fee
text: UDF/Development Fee is levied at new Greenfield and JVC airports on departing passengers. Sample rates (inclusive of all taxes): Bengaluru International Airport - Rs. 260 (domestic) / Rs. 1070 (international); Hyderabad International Airport - Rs. 375 (domestic) / Rs. 1000 (international); Delhi International Airport - Rs. 200 (domestic) / Rs. 1300 (international); Mumbai International Airport - Rs. 100 (domestic) / Rs. 600 (international), the latter two being Development Fee.

title: Purpose of Passenger Service Fee (PSF)
text: Passenger Service Fee (PSF) is levied to meet expenditure on airport security and passenger facilities at airports. It is not used to fund new development or upgradation of airports. UDF/PSF is collected as part of the passenger fare and remitted to the concerned airport operator (AAI, private airport, or JVC).

title: Definition of Development Fee
text: Development Fee is a levy made under Section 22A of the AAI Act, 1994, for funding or financing the cost of upgradation, modernization, or development of an airport. It is a 'pre-funding' charge and is consistent with ICAO policies.

title: AAI Airport Network Overview
text: Airports Authority of India (AAI) manages 115 airports in the country, including 23 civil enclaves. AAI was constituted under an Act of Parliament, the Airports Authority of India Act, 1994, as a Statutory Body.

title: International Airports in India
text: There are seventeen international airports in India. AAI-managed international airports include Netaji Subhash Chandra Bose International Airport (Kolkata), Chennai International Airport, Thiruvananthapuram International Airport, Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel International Airport (Ahmedabad), Guru Ram Dass Jee International Airport (Amritsar), Lokpriya Gopinath Bordoloi International Airport (Guwahati), Goa International Airport, Srinagar International Airport, Jaipur International Airport, Kozhikode Airport (Calicut), and Veer Savarkar International Airport (Port Blair). Privately managed international airports include Indira Gandhi International Airport (Delhi), Chhatrapati Shivaji International Airport (Mumbai), GMR Hyderabad International Airport, Bangalore International Airport, Cochin International Airport, and Dr. B.R. Ambedkar International Airport (Nagpur).

title: AAI Board Structure
text: AAI is managed by a Board of Members appointed by the Central Government under Section 3 of the AAI Act. The Board comprises a Whole-Time Chairperson, the DGCA as Ex-Officio Member, five Full-Time Members (Operations, Finance, HR, Planning, and Air Navigation Services), the Joint Secretary in-charge of AAI and AS&FA in the Ministry of Civil Aviation, and three Part-Time non-official Members.

title: AAI Miniratna Status
text: AAI has been consistently profitable since its formation. In February 2009, AAI was granted 'Miniratna Category 1 PSE' status by the Government of India, enhancing the Board's financial powers to invest capital expenditure up to Rs. 500 crores without Government approval.

title: AAI Revenue Share and Equity in JVC Airports
text: AAI holds a 26% equity share in both Delhi International Airport Ltd. (DIAL) and Mumbai International Airport Ltd. (MIAL). AAI's share of gross revenue is 45.99% in the case of DIAL and 38.7% in the case of MIAL.

title: Greenfield Airport Distance Policy
text: Per the Government of India's Policy on Airport Infrastructure (December 1999), a new Greenfield airport will normally not be allowed within 150 km of the nearest existing airport, unless set up by the Government through AAI on socio-economic grounds, in which case grant-in-aid is provided to cover capital cost and recurring losses.

title: AAI Corporate Headquarters Address
text: AAI's Corporate Headquarters is located in New Delhi at: Airports Authority of India, Corporate Headquarters, Rajiv Gandhi Bhawan, Safdarjung Airport, New Delhi - 110003. Phone: 011 24632950.

title: What is Vigilance Clearance
text: Vigilance Clearance is an instrument to certify whether an employee is involved in any misconduct or criminal offence, such as demand or acceptance of illegal gratification, possession of disproportionate assets, forgery, cheating, abuse of official position involving a vigilance angle, or violation of AAI Employees (Conduct, Discipline & Appeal) Regulations, 2003.

title: What Complaints Fall Under Vigilance
text: Complaints regarding corrupt practices such as demanding or accepting a bribe, misuse of official position for private gain, or doubtful integrity related to officials of AAI, including stakeholders, are handled by the Vigilance Department. Complaints related to officials/stakeholders and AAI service matters are only to be referred to the Vigilance Department.

title: How to File a Vigilance Complaint
text: Complaints against AAI officials can be filed in three ways: (1) online complaints on AAI's vigilance webpage with documentary proof attached as PDFs, (2) source information or verbal complaints via the toll-free number 1800-11-0402 at the office of the Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO), or (3) written complaints with supporting documents sent to: The Chief Vigilance Officer, Airports Authority of India, Corporate Headquarters, Rajiv Gandhi Bhawan, Safdarjung Airport, New Delhi - 110003.

title: Complaint Verification and Investigation Timelines
text: All complaints received are reviewed by the Chief Vigilance Officer (CVO) and ordered for verification, detailed investigation, administrative action, or filing as deemed fit. Verification of a complaint takes one month, and investigation of a complaint with a vigilance angle takes three months.

title: Anonymous Complaints Policy
text: Anonymous or pseudonymous complaints are not entertained by AAI's Vigilance Department. Complaints must be authenticated (e.g., via questionnaire or show cause notice) to be considered genuine before investigation.

title: Referral of Serious Vigilance Cases to CBI
text: Issues involving serious irregularities by AAI employees that involve external agencies are referred for investigation by the CBI, with approval of the Disciplinary Authority. Vigilance Department, AAI investigates complaints related to serving employees only.

title: Complaints Without a Vigilance Angle
text: Complaints found not to have a vigilance angle are marked to the Head of Department (HoD) concerned for further administrative action, rather than being investigated by the Vigilance Department.
